summary.name: JackMate
summary.one_liner: A native macOS app for starting, configuring and patching the JACK audio server (jackd), with a visual patchbay and menu bar control.
use_cases: Configure and start a JACK server on macOS without using the terminal
Visually route audio and MIDI between JACK clients
Save and reload a complete JACK patchbay setup
Bring native macOS apps like Safari or Music into a JACK graph
Sync multiple DAWs to a shared JACK transport and BPM
Monitor xruns and latency from the menu bar
summary.what_it_does: JackMate is a native macOS interface for the JACK Audio Connection Kit. It lets you select audio interfaces, sample rate and buffer size, computes compatible sample rates, and generates the jackd command, with options such as hog mode, channel selection, aggregate device support and a live latency readout. A visual patchbay shows active JACK clients and lets you draw connections with the mouse, with multi-select, auto-layout and Connect All. Sessions can be saved as named Studios that store connections, node positions, JACK config and CLI client commands, and restarted JACK only when the configuration has changed. The app also provides transport controls with BBT, timecode or frame display and can claim the JACK timebase master role. Version 2.0.0 adds bridging native macOS apps into the JACK graph via the JackMoebius virtual audio driver, which the page describes as a separate free 14-day trial with a one-time purchase.
notable: Visual patchbay with mouse-drawn connections and Sugiyama auto-layout
Saved Studios restore connections, config and client commands in one click
Menu bar control for start/stop, xruns and latency
2.0.0 bridges native macOS apps into the JACK graph via JackMoebius
caveats: Native app bridging depends on JackMoebius, which is a free 14-day trial then one-time purchase
Interface is in English, French, German, Italian and Spanish only; no Windows or Linux support mentioned
